For image features, we extract Faster R-CNN features with ResNet-101 backbone trained on Visual genome BIBREF4 dataset, similar to BIBREF2. We use an adaptive number of object proposals per-image ranging from 10 to 100 generated using a fixed confidence threshold and each object is then associated with 2048-dimensional mean-pooled features using ROI pooling. We use discriminative decoding throughout our models.

title: Ensemble based discriminative models for Visual Dialog Challenge 2018
answer_short: Late Fusion Encoder (LF) with Concatenated History, Memory Network Encoder (MN) with Bi-directional GRUs, Memory Network Encoder with Additional Linear Layer (Wt)
answer_rationale: Text 9 explicitly lists the three model variants used in the ensemble: 'Late Fusion Encoder (LF) with Concatenated History', 'Memory Network Encoder (MN) with Bi-directional GRUs', and 'Memory Network Encoder with Additional Linear Layer (Wt)'. These are described in detail under the 'Three Model Variants' section, and Text 2 and Text 3 confirm that the final submission is an ensemble of these three discriminative models.
